about: Women's tennis's earlier seasons (docs/design/womens-tennis.md, "Earlier seasons"): Tennis Abstract's own year-end WTA Elo reports for 2016-2025, archived by the Wayback Machine, and year-end Elo computed from Jeff Sackmann's WTA match results by Tennis Abstract's published method for 1973-2015; 1963-1972 by a second run of the method warmed up on the majors' and the Federation Cup's results of 1960-1967 from English Wikipedia's pages (wikipedia, method.early), which alone make 1963-1967. npm run sync:womens-tennis-seasons rebuilds scripts/data/womens-tennis-seasons/ from the pinned inputs (cached in the ignored data-src/womens-tennis-seasons/); npm run build:womens-tennis-seasons builds the season files from there.

wikipedia.about: The women's game before the open era, for the seasons 1963-1967 and the warm-up of 1968-1972 (method.early): English Wikipedia's article pages of the four majors' women's singles, 1960-1967 (draws), the tournaments' own articles for their dates (the women's singles' first day, from the infobox), the Federation Cup of 1963-1967 (cups), the pages of the redirects its players' links take (redirects), and Wikidata's items of the linked articles (wikidata). Every page was fetched once under /wiki/, which Wikipedia's robots.txt allows (/w/ and its API are disallowed), through scripts/lib/polite-fetch.mjs on 2026-11-14, and is pinned by its revision, SHA-256 and size; the cache is data-src/womens-tennis-seasons/wikipedia/ (each file the title, ~ and the first 8 hex digits of the title's SHA-1). A page fetched again is the current revision in Wikipedia's markup of the day, so it will not match its pin: the cache is the record. scripts/lib/tennis-wikipedia.mjs reads the pages' Parsoid HTML, where every bracket and tie is a template in a data-mw attribute.
wikipedia.licence: CC BY-SA 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/): the pages' text by Wikipedia's contributors; the results they record are facts, and nothing of their text is in a season file

redirects.about: Every linked title of the pages that Wikipedia marks as a redirect (mw-redirect), fetched under /wiki/: its page is the article it redirects to (wgRedirectedFrom, wgPageName), and the woman is that article's.

wikidata.about: The Wikidata item of every article a player cell links to (a redirect followed), from QLever's Wikidata endpoint (no robots.txt; Wikidata's own query service and API are disallowed), asked once through scripts/lib/wikidata-sparql.mjs on 2026-11-14 with the query scripts/sync-tennis-seasons.mjs builds from these titles. A woman whose item is the player file's wikidata_id of a player is that player.

wikipedia.flagsNote: The pages' flag templates name a country by its code ({{flagicon|AUS}}) or, a few times, by name: each is the manifest's code of that country (SAF is South Africa's older code). Egypt is the United Arab Republic of the day by its name of the day (src/data/namesOfTheDay.js).
wikipedia.sameCodesNote: The player file's codes that are the pages' country of the day: West Germany (FRG) is GER there, Rhodesia (RHO) ZIM, Czechoslovakia (TCH) CZE.

sources: https://www.tennisabstract.com/blog/2019/12/03/an-introduction-to-tennis-elo/ (expected score; starts in the low 1200s since challengers and qualifying were added, depending on the level)
https://www.tennisabstract.com/blog/2018/05/15/handling-injuries-and-absences/ (layoff penalty, K after a layoff, second layoffs, the 1900 study population, the offseason not counted)
K = 250 / (matches + 5)^0.4 is FiveThirtyEight's formula, which Sackmann said he adapted (sleepomeno/tennis_atp examples/elo.R); his own worked example and the February 2016 report fit an offset of 6

start.fit: Not published: the tour-level start fitted on Tennis Abstract's own current-method numbers for 1973-2000, the career peaks of the 17 women of its Tennis 128 profiles whose peaks fall then; the start of an ITF event, a WTA 125 or a qualifying round is the men's, which keeps the 2021-2025 lists within ten points of Tennis Abstract's. Before 1994 the files name no ITF event's prize, so a newcomer's first counted match is at tour level, and the men's 1450 there lifts the 1970s and 1980s by about 100 points.

layoff.note: A layoff of eight weeks or more between counted matches, 15 November to 15 January not counted, costs 100 points rising linearly to 150 at a year; K is then 1.5 times as large, back to normal over 20 matches; a second layoff within two years of the last comeback is charged the difference between the penalty for both together and for the first. Charged on return; a list shows a player in the middle of one with the penalty he would be charged on the list's date. Only for players rated 1900 or more, as in the study that set it (applied to everyone it lowers the whole list by 100 to 200 points against every published number).

method.counted: Tour-level main draws with the Fed Cup and Billie Jean King Cup (wta_matches_<year>.csv: not its exhibitions, junior events or ITF circuits under $50K), tour-level qualifying, and the main draws of the WTA 125s (level C from 2012) and of ITF events of $50K or more (wta_matches_qual_itf_<year>.csv), as Tennis Abstract's report says ("tour-level, tour-level qualifying ... or ITF $50K+"): not the qualifying of a 125 or an ITF event, nor any ITF event before 1994, whose prize the files do not name; nor a walkover, retirement, default, abandoned or unfinished match, nor one without a score or against a placeholder opponent.
method.order: By the files' season, then the event's date, the event, the round (qualifying first) and the match number: a season ends after its last event and before the next season's first, even one that starts in late December.
method.activityNote: A season lists the women who played at least 10 counted matches in it, as Tennis Abstract's report lists those with 10 in the last 52 weeks. The published seasons keep the women of Tennis Abstract's list who pass the same test in the match files.
method.asOf: A list is dated 31 December, or the start of the season's last event when that is later.

peaks.source: Tennis Abstract, The Tennis 128 (2022): each player's peak Elo by the current method, from her profile

v1.note: Tennis Abstract's method before May 2018, for the check against its 2016 and 2017 reports: tour-level matches only, everyone starting at 1500, no layoff penalty.

early.about: The women's seasons before 1973 (docs/design/womens-tennis.md, "1963-1967"): a second run of this method, kept apart from the first so that 1973-2025 rebuild byte for byte. It reads the four majors' women's singles and the Federation Cup of 1960-1967 from English Wikipedia's pages (wikipedia, above) before the open era's files, its newcomers of the pages starting at their own level and its layoffs before the open era charged only from amateurWeeks, and snapshots 1963-1972 (seasons.early). The rest is the method above.
early.results: English Wikipedia: the majors' women's singles draws and the Federation Cup
early.method: Tennis Abstract's published Elo method, warmed up on the majors' and the Federation Cup's results of 1960-1967 from English Wikipedia (docs/design/womens-tennis.md, "1963-1967")
early.counted: Every played singles match of the pages: the majors' draws and the cup's singles rubbers (rubbers 1 and 2; the doubles, rubber 3, rate nobody), never a walkover, a retirement or a default (the scores' w/o, ret., def. and a retirement's superscript r). A match that the finals bracket and a section both show is counted once. Rounds are numbered back from each bracket's last (scripts/lib/tennis-wikipedia.mjs); the cup's by its days, its last day the final. A major's matches are dated the first day of its women's singles, a cup rubber its tie's day.

start.fit: Not published: a newcomer whose first counted match is on the pages starts at 1325, fitted to five points so that the run carries on as the shipped one. Over the shipped run's top 50 of each season 1973-1980 its Elo of the same women differs from the shipped run's by +0.1 on average (at most 0.5 in a season); on Tennis Abstract's 17 targets for 1973-2000 (targets above) it comes out -0.3 Elo on average, root mean square 42.8 (the shipped run: -0.4 and 42.7). 1320 puts the seam at -0.4, 1330 at +1.4, 1280 at -9.5 and 1380 at +14.8 (with the layoffs below); Tingay's tens agree as well with any of them.

layoff.note: The open era's rule (layoff above) for every gap that begins on or after 1 January 1968. A gap that begins and ends before it is charged on the same scale only when it lasts 13 weeks or more: the pages hold the majors and the cup alone, so the eight-week rule charges most gaps between them. Against Tingay's tens of 1963-1967 (checks below) the mean rank correlation is 0.72 with eight weeks, 0.76 with 13, 0.72 with 26, 0.72 with 39 and 0.72 with no charge (start 1325): one season, 1967, makes the difference. A gap across the start (Court's of 1967, her year away) is never charged.

activity.note: 1963-1967 (seasons.amateur) list the women with three counted matches in the season, or a played singles rubber in that year's Federation Cup, the user's choice of 2026-11-14 so that every cup nation fields the women who played it; 1968-1972 ten, as from 1973. The pages hold the majors and the cup alone: at three matches alone, 41 of the 82 cup nations of 1963-1967 had two rated cup players, with the cup's rubbers all 82.

early.nations: A woman of 1963-1967 plays for her fix, else her cup nation of the nearest season (the first run's rule, the pages' cups and the match files' together), else the country her draws' flags give her in the nearest season of the pages (within cupWindow), else the player file's; from 1968 the first run's rule.

aliases.note: Keys of one woman, reviewed by hand on 2026-11-14, the merged key's matches counted under the kept one. A key is a linked article (a redirect followed), a red link's title, or a name written without a link and its country (Name|CODE). Rule 'name': the same plain name in one country, checked by scripts/lib/tennis-wikipedia.mjs; 'spelling': a spelling of the same name, why given. Not merged: Margot Anne Smith (New Zealand) and Margaret Smith Court; Pauline and Pat Roberts, who played each other; Alison Martin (Australia) and Andrée Martin (Canada); Irène and Isabelle de Lansalut, Madonna and Maree Schacht, María Tort de Ayala and Maria Ayala, with nothing to show either pair is one woman.
items: Carol and Carole: one Australian, at the 1962 and 1963 Australian Championships
Lyn and Lynn: one Australian, at the 1962, 1964 and 1966 Australian Championships
The red link's title garbles é as ú (as other titles of these pages garble è as þ): one Spaniard, María José Aubet
Her initials: the same Spaniard at the 1967 French Championships
With and without her middle initial: one American, in 1967
The red link's title misspells Patsy: one New Zealander, at the 1962 Australian Championships

joins.note: Women of the pages who are the player file's, so that they carry on into the open era's files under its id, reviewed by hand on 2026-11-14; a woman whose article's Wikidata item is a player's wikidata_id needs no row. Rule 'name': her key's name or a name her cells show is the player file's, plainly, in one country (sameCodes), checked by scripts/lib/tennis-wikipedia.mjs. Not joined: Maria Ayala (Chile, 1960) and the player file's Maria Ayala (Puerto Rico), Mary Habicht (the United States) and its Mary Habicht (Brazil): one name, two countries.

nations.note: A computed season's player plays for the nation she played the Fed Cup for in the nearest season (the same season first, then earlier, then later, within six seasons), from the ties' names in the match files ("Fed Cup WG F: USA vs AUS"), else for her country by the player file, which gives only her latest; then as the state of that season knew it. A published season's player plays for the country Tennis Abstract's rankings report of the nearest date files her under, else for her country by the player file.

barred.name: South Africa
barred.why: Barred over apartheid: the match files have no South African Fed Cup tie from 1978 until 1992.

barred.name: FR Yugoslavia
barred.why: Barred by the United Nations sanctions: the match files have no Yugoslav Fed Cup tie in 1993 or 1994; it is back in 1995.

fixes.name: Martina Navratilova
fixes.why: Defected from Czechoslovakia in September 1975 and lived in the United States, an American from 1981; her Fed Cup rows are Czechoslovakia's in 1975 and the United States' from 1982, so the nearest-season rule would keep her Czechoslovak to 1978.

fixes.name: Hana Mandlikova
fixes.why: Australian from January 1988; her Fed Cup rows are Czechoslovakia's, the last in 1987, so the nearest-season rule would keep her Czechoslovak to the end.

fixes.name: Monica Seles
fixes.why: Yugoslav until she became an American in 1994; her Fed Cup rows are the United States' from 1996, and the player file lists her as American.

fixes.name: Rosalyn Fairbank
fixes.why: South African: her Fed Cup rows are South Africa's (1993); the player file lists her as American, her later country.

fixes.name: Hu Na
fixes.why: Defected in July 1982 and was granted asylum in the United States in 1983; her Fed Cup rows are China's (1981-1982), so the nearest-season rule would keep her Chinese to 1988.

dayNations.note: Vietnam's cup team to 1975 was the Republic of Vietnam's (South Vietnam, Wikipedia, revision 1384578494: the fall of Saigon on 30 April 1975); the Democratic Republic of Vietnam played neither cup. On the map of those years South Vietnam is a shape of its own (docs/design/historic-maps.md).

checks.about: Published judgments of the seasons before 1973, kept as validation inputs only: validation.json's checks compare the computed lists with them, and nothing from them is in a season file.
